www.xbox.com.role_confirmed_this_stage: product_page (commercial storefront) -- confirmed: the fetched root redirected within-host to a locale homepage, and a sitemap-discovered URL (/en-us/consoles/xbox-series-s) is a real Product-Detail-Page-style listing with purchase options, pricing CTAs, and full technical specifications
www.xbox.com.ownership_evidence_this_stage: Page content includes the Microsoft "UHF" (universal header/footer) corporate component -- the same shared footer framework used across microsoft.com properties -- with a "Microsoft corporate links" nav section and a link to https://www.microsoft.com/trademarks. Combined with Stage 10's original provenance (linked from the already-verified support.microsoft.com official navigation), this is now content-verified, not just link-provenance.

support.xbox.com.role_confirmed_this_stage: support -- confirmed: robots.txt and a 2,973-URL en-US sitemap describe a help/support article structure (help/hardware-network/..., help/games-apps/..., etc.), consistent with a support role, not a commercial storefront
support.xbox.com.ownership_evidence_this_stage: Sitemap structure and URL naming are internally consistent with an official Xbox support portal; the two hardware-setup articles found by URL (unbox-xbox-series-xs-console, set-up-new-series-x-s) are exactly the kind of content an official support site would host for this exact console family.
support.xbox.com.content_access_blocker: Every fetched page on this host (root and both candidate articles) is a bare React SPA shell (~2,897 bytes, <noscript>You need to enable JavaScript to run this app.</noscript>) -- no server-rendered article text is reachable by a static bounded GET. Chromium/browser automation is explicitly out of scope for this stage, so this host's actual help content could not be read.

variant_evidence.source_discovery_method: listed verbatim in the official https://www.xbox.com/sitemap/cms-sitemap-0.xml.gz content sitemap chunk (declared in www.xbox.com/robots.txt), not guessed
variant_evidence.explicit_spec_line_pairing_color_and_cap: XBOX Series S Robot White: 512GB Custom NVME SSD | XBOX Series S Carbon Black: 1TB Custom NVME SSD | XBOX Series S Robot White: 1TB Custom NVME SSD
variant_evidence.matches_target_variant: 1TB All-Digital Carbon Black -- capacity (1TB) AND color (Carbon Black) both match, together, in one named option, not inferred separately
not_confused_with: 512GB Robot White (base/white capacity variant) -- different color AND different capacity, explicitly a separate option on the same page
1TB Robot White (white 1TB variant) -- same capacity as target but different color, explicitly a separate option on the same page
variant_evidence.caveat: The official page never displays a manufacturer/region SKU code (e.g. no "RRS-00011"/"XXU-00015"-style string anywhere in the fetched content). Matching to the catalog row is therefore by model + capacity + color descriptive consistency, exactly as Stage 9.1 established for the PlayStation controller -- this is the strongest evidence available, not proof of an exact code-level match. Per instructions, the seller article is not expected to appear on the official page and its absence is not itself evidence of anything.

criterion_1_brand_model_confirmed_by_off.detail: Brand and exact model (Xbox Series S) confirmed on www.xbox.com.

criterion_2_catalog_row_linked_to_confir.detail: Linked by model+capacity+color descriptive consistency to the "1TB All-Digital Carbon Black" official option; no conflicting field found; manufacturer code not confirmable (expected).

criterion_3_official_matched_image_confi.detail: 3 images explicitly labeled "Carbon-Aware" found on the confirmed page.

criterion_4_specifications_sufficient.detail: CPU, GPU, memory, storage, I/O, video, sound, ports, dimensions, and weight all found with a variant-specific storage/color pairing.

criterion_5_manual_confirmed_present_or_.detail: Neither confirmed present nor confirmed absent -- candidate articles exist but are JS-only and unreadable within this stage's no-Chromium constraint.

export_readiness_reason: Criteria 1-4 now pass, a substantial change from Stage 10 (which failed at criterion 1). The sole remaining blocker is criterion 5: the instruction manual cannot be confirmed present or absent, because the only host serving support content (support.xbox.com) is a JavaScript-only SPA that this stage is not permitted to render. This is a structural access blocker, not a missing-data gap -- the candidate article URLs are known and could be revisited by a future stage with a different, explicitly authorized capability (e.g. a manual, user-directed Chromium diagnostic session, per this project's existing browser-tooling policy) if the user wants that pursued.
